title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography featuring non-consensual sexual imagery of real people was deployed on a platform with millions of monthly visitors. The system used generative AI to create these videos without the consent or knowledge of the people depicted. The failure was a complete absence of deployment safeguards: no checks prevented the creation or distribution of non-consensual sexual content, and no human review filtered what the platform hosted.

This is a case of a system built and deployed for an inherently harmful purpose. Catch it would have required the platform to implement detection systems for non-consensual sexual imagery, content moderation to remove such material, and user verification to prevent anonymous uploads designed to evade accountability. It would also have required legal and policy frameworks that existed before deployment to be enforced.

It is not established whether the platform's operators created the deepfake technology themselves or merely hosted content created elsewhere.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos posted on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains deepfake pornography featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed they have filed complaints or are considering legal proceedings.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto explicit content, is classified as revenge porn and is illegal. Users who upload this material are advised to remain anonymous to avoid prosecution and receive payment based on video views. Lawyers recommend victims file reports with authorities, who can attempt to shut down the websites. Other options include starting a mass lawsuit, filing complaints with the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued action against her deepfake videos, resulting in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
